Using the standard abundance identity

\[
[X/Y]=[X/H]-[Y/H],
\]

for Star 1,

\[
[\mathrm{Si/H}]_1=[\mathrm{Si/Fe}]_1+[\mathrm{Fe/H}]_1
=0.3+0=0.3.
\]

For Star 2,

\[
[\mathrm{Mg/Si}]_2=[\mathrm{Mg/H}]_2-[\mathrm{Si/H}]_2,
\]

so

\[
0.3=0-[\mathrm{Si/H}]_2
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
[\mathrm{Si/H}]_2=-0.3.
\]

Therefore, the ratio of silicon number abundances is

\[
\frac{(n_{\rm Si}/n_{\rm H})_1}{(n_{\rm Si}/n_{\rm H})_2}
=10^{[\mathrm{Si/H}]_1-[\mathrm{Si/H}]_2}
=10^{0.3-(-0.3)}
=10^{0.6}
\approx 3.98\approx 3.9.
\]

The stellar masses and solar Fe and Mg abundances cancel out in this abundance-ratio calculation.

Answer: D
